To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
12- nt RNA species derived from mature microRNAs (termed smiRNAs) modulate the activity of the microRNA precursor from which they are derived.
the 12 nt RNA species generated during the microRNA pathway can modulate microRNA function.
the 5′ end of the mature microRNAs, generated along the Dicer processing pathway, are not degraded, but rather are released from the precursor as 12-nt smiRNA species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a new class of small RNA species, the semi-microRNAs, and their role in gene regulation.
microRNA biogenesis, a complex and poorly understood process.

microRNA processing and function, and we have uncovered an additional layer of control of microRNA activity by a short RNA species derived from the precursor microRNA, which we term semi-microRNA (smiRNA)
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
microRNAs are processed from their precursors into 19–24 nt small RNAs that can be cleaved into smaller 12-nt fragments.
the 12 nt long RNA species are devoid of direct mRNA regulatory activity.
smiRNAs do not have an independent role in mRNA regulation but modulate the activity of the microRNAs from which they are derived.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
microRNA biogenesis generates two different RNA species with distinct activities, the microRNA and the smiRNA.
microRNAs are not alone and they are not alone in their action.
the 5′ arm of the precursor microRNA is not a waste product of the microRNA pathway but rather an active player.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microRNAs are not the only species that can be generated from a precursor, as we have shown that a microRNA can give rise to an additional 12-nt species, the so-called smiRNAs.
the 5′ end of a microRNA is sufficient to modulate its activity in a cell-free system.
microRNAs are not the only players in the RNA-mediated gene silencing pathway.
